## Rule

Each input is a square active grid (20x20 through 30x30) with exactly three
same-color nonzero markers on a 45-degree diagonal, equally spaced. The middle
marker is the center. The spacing between adjacent markers is the period. For
each active-grid cell, compute Chebyshev distance from the center; output the
marker color exactly when that distance is a multiple of the period, otherwise
background. Padding outside the active square must remain all-zero.

## Algorithm sketch

Reference recipe: `Research_Archive/notes/recipe-task137-diagonal-marker-square-rings.md`.

Compact ONNX sketch used by `prototypes/build_task137_v1.py`: derive active
side length as `sqrt(ReduceSum(input))`; use scalar `Einsum` moments over the
three nonzero markers to recover color sum, center row/col, and period from row
variance; run 1D INT8/UINT8 distance and modulo chains on rows and columns; use
a full 30x30 Chebyshev axis selector to choose row vs column ring state; assemble
a single UINT8 color-index canvas and expand to BOOL one-hot with final
`Equal(canvas, channel_ids)`. The canvas stores `3*color`, so the final palette
is `[0,3,6,...,27]` and sentinel `64` decodes as all-zero padding.

## Cost analysis

_Why is the current cost what it is? What ops dominate? Are there cheaper expressions of the same rule? Link a session log if you've measured._

2026-06-01 current v1 cost 2,516 is dominated by two unavoidable-looking
full-canvas intermediates: `row_gt_b` BOOL = 900 and `canvas_u8` UINT8 = 900.
Everything else is skinny: row/col arithmetic is 30-byte INT8/UINT8/BOOL
vectors, and marker decoding is scalar moment math. Params are 114 elements:
row/col INT8 index vectors (60), shared F32 0..29 index (30), channel weights
(10), scaled channel ids (10), and scalar constants. The row-square moment
reuses the shared F32 index twice in one `Einsum`, so no separate row-square
initializer is needed. Sub-1k would require eliminating both full-canvas
intermediates or fusing Chebyshev axis-select + color expansion into the graph
output, which current scoreable ORT ops do not expose.

2026-06-01 under-2k audit: with both `row_gt_b` and `canvas_u8` retained, the
hard lower bound is already 1,800 + 114 params = 1,914 before the 602 bytes of
required scalar/1D marker, active, distance, modulo, and padding-sentinel
plumbing. So cost <2,000 requires deleting or fusing at least one full 30x30
plane. Replacing only `canvas_u8` with skinny row/col one-hot branches does not
cross the line: the scoreable UINT8-branch final `Where` scored 2,702, and the
hypothetical BOOL-branch version is rejected by ORT. Replacing only `row_gt_b`
would be enough on paper, but every exact route found so far materializes an
equivalent full selector, full ring mask, or larger sparse/channel expansion.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

2026-06-01: Do not stop at whole-input `Cast(input→UINT8)` plus full `[1,9,30,30]` non-bg slice. That variant verified byte-equal but cost 27,336; replacing it with F32 active + narrow row/col projections gets the same behavior at 13,363.

2026-06-01: Do not use row/col sentinel vectors with the raw `row_gt = row_dist > col_dist` condition. It scored 5,345 but only matched LIVE 35/266 because padding cells can choose the still-active axis. The fixed version adjusts inactive row/col distances upward before the axis select and scores 3,727 after switching row/col detection to Conv reducers.

2026-06-01: Do not retry the all-INT8 distance path. ONNX shape-check accepts
it, but ORT/scorer rejects `Where` over INT8. The working compromise is INT8
delta/abs followed by `Cast` to UINT8 before `Where`, `Mod`, and `Equal`.

2026-06-01: Do not replace the final `canvas_u8 -> Equal(channel_ids)` with
skinny BOOL row/col branches plus final `Where`: ORT rejects `Where` over BOOL.
Casting those branches to UINT8 costs four 300-byte skinny tensors, worse than
the 900-byte canvas. Also do not use final `OneHot`; ORT rejects `OneHot(11)` in
the official scorer path.

2026-06-01: Do not remove period rounding after `Sqrt(row_var * 1.5)`. It scores
slightly cheaper but fails (`verify_against_live` 175/266, truth 6476/10000)
because `Sqrt` under-rounds some perfect-square periods before the UINT8 cast.
Center rounding can stay removed; center ratios are exact integer divisions in
F32 for the marker-coordinate range.

2026-06-01: The `Where(mask, paint, input)` output-overlay trick from
Onnx_Advanced is not cheaper here. Task137 would still need a full ring mask;
the current canvas formulation combines ring/background/padding into one
900-byte UINT8 plane and avoids materializing a separate full BOOL ring mask.

2026-06-01: Do not retry direct final row/col one-hot branch selection. The
scoreable form `Equal(row_value, channel_ids)`/`Equal(col_value, channel_ids)`
then `Cast(..., UINT8)` then final `Where(row_gt, row_branch, col_branch)`
removes `canvas_u8` but adds 1,200 bytes of skinny branch tensors and scores
2,702. The cleaner BOOL branch form would be about 2,247, but ORT rejects
`Where(BOOL, BOOL, BOOL)` (`Could not find an implementation for Where(9)`).

2026-06-01: Do not ship the no-period-guard probe despite real-input
correctness. It removes `Max(period_u8_raw, one_u8)` and passes visible/truth
because valid generator inputs always have nonzero period, but
`score_network_v2` uses a ch0-only dummy input with no marker color. That dummy
drives integer `Mod(..., 0)` and native-crashes/rejects scoring (`rc=3221225620`).

2026-06-01: Sparse initializer probes are not useful here. Sparse row/col/index
initializers make shape inference reject `Less`/`Einsum`, sparse `channel_ids`
is rejected by `Equal`, and sparse `channel_weights`/`row_idx_f32` make the
`Einsum` shape inference lose rank information.
